items.title: feat(devtools): add nested data search
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

Adds case-insensitive search for nested property names and primitive values in the query and mutation Data Explorer. Matching branches and the first matching page open automatically. Clear or Escape restores manual expansion.

Uses the CSS Custom Highlight API for matching text. Editable query values have a highlighted input.

Related to https://github.com/TanStack/query/discussions/11033.

Validation:
- `pnpm run test:pr --uncommitted` passed for all 142 affected projects.
- Browser checks covered native highlights, editable values, Shadow DOM, and cleanup.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Search query and mutation data in the Data Explorer, including nested property names and primitive values in Maps and Sets. Search is case-insensitive, highlights matches, and automatically expands matching branches.
  * For paginated data, the first page with a match opens automatically; other pages with matches are highlighted. Up to 1,000 matches are highlighted at a time.
  * Clear a search or press Escape to restore manual expansion. Selecting a different query or mutation clears the search.
  * Query data remains editable during search, but bulk editing is unavailable while search is active. Mutation data remains read-only.
* **Documentation**
  * Added guidance on searching query and mutation data.

items.title: fix(vue-query/queryClient): preserve union narrowing in 'setQueryData' updaters for tagged query keys
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

- Type the updater input of the tagged query key overload of `setQueryData` in `packages/vue-query/src/queryClient.ts` as `InferDataFromTag<NoInfer<TQueryFnData>, TTaggedQueryKey> | undefined`, the same as `@tanstack/query-core`. With `NoInfer<TInferredQueryFnData>`, a discriminated union narrowed inside the updater did not match the overload (`No overload matches this call`).
- Add the `should preserve discriminated union narrowing in setQueryData updaterFn` type test to `packages/vue-query/src/__tests__/queryOptions.test-d.ts`.
- Add a patch changeset for `@tanstack/vue-query`.

items.title: chore(*): update Angular to v22 and TypeScript to v6 in Angular examples and integration
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

Update Angular to v22 for the Angular packages' dev environment, the Angular examples and the Angular integration.

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog (used by the `devDependencies` of `@tanstack/angular-query-experimental` and `@tanstack/angular-query-persist-client`):
  - `@angular/{common,compiler,core,platform-browser}`: `^20.0.0` → `^22.2.4`
  - `@testing-library/angular`: `^18.0.0` → `^19.6.0` (v19 requires Angular `>=21`)
  - `peerDependencies` (`>=16.0.0`) are unchanged.
- `examples/angular/*` (11 examples):
  - `@angular/*`: `^20.0.0` → `^22.2.4`, `@angular/build` and `@angular/cli`: `^22.2.5`
  - `typescript`: `5.8.3` → `^6.0.3`
  - Remove `zone.js` from `dependencies` and the `zone.js` entry from `polyfills` in `angular.json`. None of the examples call `provideZoneChangeDetection`, so they already run zoneless on Angular v22, which is the default for new Angular v22 apps.
- Replace `integrations/angular/cli-20` with `integrations/angular/cli-22`, regenerated with Angular CLI v22.2.5 (`ng new` with inline template/style and no tests), keeping the existing customizations (disabled analytics and cache, the `injectQuery` app, `provideTanStackQuery`):
  - `@angular/*`: `^22.2.4`, `@angular/build` and `@angular/cli`: `^22.2.5`, `typescript`: `^6.0.3`, no `zone.js`
  - The generated `tsconfig.json` no longer sets `strict`, `strictTemplates` and `typeCheckHostBindings`, which are enabled by default in TypeScript v6 and Angular v22.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: Angular v20, `esbuild@0.25.9`, `esbuild@0.25.12` and `vite@7.1.11` are no longer in the lockfile, so `esbuild` resolves to a single `0.28.2`.

items.title: fix({react,preact,angular,solid,vue}-query/infiniteQueryOptions): correct the overload selected for a possibly-undefined 'initialData'
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

`DefinedInitialDataInfiniteOptions['initialData']` (the overload selected when `initialData` is set, meant to guarantee `data` is never `undefined`) incorrectly included `| undefined` in `packages/react-query/src/infiniteQueryOptions.ts`, `packages/preact-query/src/infiniteQueryOptions.ts`, and `packages/angular-query-experimental/src/infinite-query-options.ts`.

This let expressions like `initialData: id ? {...} : undefined` match the `Defined` overload, causing `useInfiniteQuery`/`injectInfiniteQuery` to infer `data` as never `undefined` even though it could be `undefined` at runtime.

Root cause: `initialData?: undefined | NonUndefinedGuard<...> | InitialDataFunction<...>` was already added to `UndefinedInitialDataInfiniteOptions` (the correct overload for this case) in an earlier PR. A later PR aiming to support the same ternary pattern missed that and added `| undefined` to the `Defined` overload instead, where it didn't belong.

Verified by removing `| undefined` and confirming, via `tsc --build`, that `initialData: id ? {...} : undefined` now falls through to `UndefinedInitialDataInfiniteOptions` as intended, and `data` is correctly typed as possibly `undefined`. Existing `.test-d` suites in all three packages still pass unmodified.

`solid-query` and `vue-query` had the opposite problem: their `UndefinedInitialDataInfiniteOptions['initialData']` was only `undefined`, so the same ternary matched neither overload and was rejected with "No overload matches this call" (in solid for both `infiniteQueryOptions` and `useInfiniteQuery`, in vue for `infiniteQueryOptions`). #8157 widened this type in `react-query` only; `preact-query`, `angular-query-experimental`, and `svelte-query` have the same shape, but solid and vue never got it. Both now accept `undefined | NonUndefinedGuard<...> | InitialDataFunction<...>`, matching the other adapters. In `vue-query`, `infiniteQueryOptions` declared the `Undefined` overload before the `Defined` one, so once `Undefined` accepted a defined `initialData` it would have been selected first and typed `options.initialData` as possibly `undefined`; the `Defined` overload is now declared first, as in the other adapters, with a test covering it.

`svelte-query` already had both overloads right, and `lit-query`'s `infiniteQueryOptions` has no `Defined`/`Undefined` overload split, so neither is affected.

Added a regression test to each of the five packages' `infiniteQueryOptions.test-d` suite asserting `data` stays `T | undefined` when `initialData` is a ternary that can evaluate to `undefined`.

items.title: fix(solid-query/{queryOptions,useQuery}): correct the overload selected for 'initialData'
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

`solid-query`'s `queryOptions`/`useQuery` resolved an `initialData` that may be `undefined` differently from the other adapters:

- `UndefinedInitialDataOptions['initialData']` only accepted `undefined`.
- `DefinedInitialDataOptions['initialData']` was `TQueryFnData | (() => TQueryFnData)`, without `NonUndefinedGuard`.

So `initialData: cond ? value : undefined` (or a function that can return `undefined`) didn't fit the `Undefined` overload and instead selected the `Defined` one, with `TQueryFnData` inferred as `T | undefined`. `data` still came out as `T | undefined`, but the query key was tagged with `T | undefined` instead of `T`.

This aligns both types with `react-query`/`preact-query`: `UndefinedInitialDataOptions['initialData']` is now `undefined | InitialDataFunction<NonUndefinedGuard<TQueryFnData>> | NonUndefinedGuard<TQueryFnData>`, and `DefinedInitialDataOptions['initialData']` uses `NonUndefinedGuard`. A possibly-undefined `initialData` now selects the `Undefined` overload and the query key is tagged with `T`.

`useQuery` declared the `Undefined` overload before the `Defined` one; with `Undefined` widened, that order would let it take a defined `initialData` too and type `data` as possibly `undefined`. The `Defined` overload is now declared first (both overload blocks are moved as-is), as in `react-query`'s `useQuery`. `data` types are unchanged for every case.

items.title: fix(vue-query/queryClient): infer the data and error types of 'getQueryState' from a tagged query key
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

The `getQueryState` override in vue-query's `QueryClient` only had the `MaybeRefDeep<QueryKey>` signature, so a key tagged by `queryOptions` gave `QueryState<unknown, Error>`, unlike `getQueryData` and the query-core `getQueryState`.

```ts
const { queryKey } = queryOptions({ queryKey: ['key'], queryFn: () => 5 })

queryClient.getQueryData(queryKey) // number | undefined
queryClient.getQueryState(queryKey)?.data // before: unknown, after: number | undefined
```

- Add an overload that infers the data and error types from a tagged key, with the same signature as query-core, and keep the `MaybeRefDeep<QueryKey>` signature for ref keys.
- Add type tests for a tagged key (data and error), an untagged key, an explicit generic, a ref key, and a `queryOptions` key.

items.title: fix({preact,solid,svelte,angular-query-experimental}): switch to 'export type *' for type-only re-exports
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

Port #11228 (react-query) to the other adapters whose `types.ts` is pure type-only: change `export * from './types'` to `export type * from './types'` in `preact-query`, `solid-query`, `svelte-query` (`types.js` only — `context.js` still re-exports runtime functions, left unchanged), and `angular-query-experimental`.

Under this repo's `isolatedModules: true`, `export *` from a type-only module cannot be safely elided by the compiler and is preserved as a real runtime import. `export type *` is erased entirely. Verified locally:
- `preact-query` and `svelte-query`: build output drops a real `import "./types.js"` / `export * from './types.js'` before vs. after this change.
- `solid-query` and `angular-query-experimental`: their bundlers (single-file tsdown bundle, vite/rollup) already tree-shook this away, so build output is unchanged — this is a source-level correctness fix for those two, not a measured bundle-size win.
- `.d.ts` output for `preact-query` is unchanged in the set of exported identifiers (each gains a `type` prefix only); a minimal consumer repro confirms this has no effect on how types are imported/used downstream.

items.title: fix(react-query*): declare '@types/react' as an optional peer dependency
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

The published type declarations of `react-query`, `react-query-devtools`, `react-query-next-experimental` and `react-query-persist-client` import React types, so strict package managers need `@types/react` to be declared. It should be optional, so JavaScript users don't get it auto-installed or see a missing peer warning.

- Declare `"@types/react": "^18 || ^19"` as a peer dependency of `react-query`, `react-query-next-experimental` and `react-query-persist-client`. `react-query-devtools` already declares it.
- Mark `@types/react` optional in `peerDependenciesMeta` in all four packages.
- In `knip.ts`, read the ignored dependencies from the optional peer dependencies, like `angular-query-experimental` does for its optional dependencies, since knip's strict mode excludes optional peers. This replaces the hard-coded `'@types/react!'` of `react-query`, `react-query-next-experimental` and `react-query-persist-client`, and adds the same for `react-query-devtools`. Removing a declaration still fails the check.
